react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome implicates a convergent disruption of sulfur amino acid metabolism and the glutathione system. RaMP multi-database ORA identified Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859) as the top hit (FDR=1.24e-6) with four compounds: coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine, and glutathione. Sulfur amino acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1614635, FDR=3.09e-4) captured hypotaurine and glutathione as co-hit members. The Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently converged on methionine and cysteine metabolism (p=0.0135), with glutathione and hypotaurine as the overlapping compounds — a direct cross-paradigm replication. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently validated Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430, p=0.02), with hypotaurine as the sole driver metabolite. The simultaneous perturbation of hypotaurine, beta-mercaptoethanol, 6-methylthiopurine, and glutathione — all sulfur-containing compounds — points to a selective stress on the trans-sulfuration pathway and phase-II detoxification capacity. Azathioprine ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR=1.38e-4) was also enriched, linking 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione through S-methyltransferase and glutathione S-transferase reactions. The presence of benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (a DNA-damaging carcinogen metabolite) alongside coumarin suggests oxidative stress from xenobiotic exposure may be the upstream trigger driving glutathione consumption.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites identified convergent hits across sulfur-amino-acid metabolism and phase-I/II xenobiotic detoxification. RaMP multi-database ORA (REACT + WikiPathways) ranked Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=1.24e-6) as the top hit, with four metabolites — coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine, and glutathione — as the driver compounds. The same ORA flagged Degradation of cysteine and homocysteine (REACT:R-HSA-1614558, FDR=1.38e-4) and Azathioprine ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR=1.38e-4) as independent sulfur-network hits. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed hypotaurine as the sole significant hit in Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430, p=0.0249). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis reproduced methionine and cysteine metabolism (p=0.007) with both hypotaurine and glutathione as overlapping driver metabolites, providing direct cross-paradigm replication. The four-sulfur metabolome signature — hypotaurine, 6-methylthiopurine, beta-mercaptoethanol, and glutathione — converges on cysteine-homocysteine catabolism and methylation capacity as the primary biological perturbation.
